Appreciate the detailed list, Tom — good signal. Short answers and follow-ups below: 

1) Rate limits / throughput:
- Default hosted plan (self-serve) is conservative; for enterprise evals we typically provision a trial with increased limits. For your POC I can provision a trial key with 1,000 req/min sustained and burst to 2,500 for short windows, and concurrency to support ~50 simultaneous streams. If you need higher sustained throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated.

2) Latency:
- For chat prompts in US region on our verified medium-latency model, p50 ~80–120ms per token; p95 varies by model and size — for the prompt/response sizes you mentioned expect p95 end-to-end ~300–800ms depending on model and sequence length. We'll provide a perf profile for the exact model you pick.

3) Data residency & retention:
- Hosted API keeps short-term logs for debugging by default. We can set retention to 7 days for your trial and disable longer-term retention; for strict residency or dedicated log control we can discuss Private deployment or Dedicated with private logging options.

4) Path to Dedicated/Private:
- Transition path is straightforward: once POC shows the need, we provision Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) or Private VPC for isolation — typical lead time ~4–8 weeks depending on contract and sizing. We'll surface costs and timelines early.

Neha will drop the quickstart + SOC2 summary in the next email and can provision the trial key once you confirm the model family and a target qps/concurrency.

Proposed next call: 30-min security/infra sync — I can do Tue May 4 at 10am PT. Works for you?

Cheers,
Aditya

On a separate note — attached: SOC2_Summary.pdf (neha will also send the full quickstart).

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Hosted API quickstart + SOC2 summary

Hi Tom —

Attaching a short quickstart and SOC2 summary to help your security and infra teams. Below are the most useful snippets to get started: 

1) Quickstart (curl):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TRIAL_KEY>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize..."}],"stream":false}'

2) Streaming: pass "stream":true and read chunked server-sent events; we support chunk-level backpressure.

3) Rate-limit headers returned on every response:
- X-RateLimit-Limit: total allowed per minute
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: remaining in window
- X-RateLimit-Reset: unix timestamp for window reset

4) Recommended test config for your POC: start with 1,000 req/min, validate latency under your payload, then scale to 2,500 burst. If you see sustained >2,000 req/min we recommend Dedicated.

Attachments included:
- Hosted_API_Quickstart_Guide.pdf (examples, SDK snippets, error handling)
- SOC2_Summary.pdf (high-level control matrix)
- sample-quickstart-repo-link.txt (link to sample GitHub repo)

I can also spin up a test key for Acme with the bumped quotas — Aditya, tell me the model choice and expiry window and I will provision.

Thanks,
